### ① Derived judgments

**Accept-set and public surface: no change, and the PR says none — right.** The diff touches `docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md` only. No Zod schema, no export, no runtime line, no generated artifact moves; the root manifest is `private: true` and no package's `files` field reaches `docs/adr` (`@objectstack/spec` ships `dist`, `json-schema`, `liveness`, `prompts`, `api-surface`, `spec-changes.json`, `protocol-upgrade-guide.md` and the like — no docs). The accept-set the runtime enforces is the one `origin/main` already enforces.

**Every clause of the new amendment note, judged against the code at `origin/main`:**

- *The third disjunct* — the door replays E when the floor is below the runtime label, OR the floor is at or below `E.retiredAfter`, OR the floor is `M.0.0` and `E.toMajor` is M. Right: the module docblock states exactly this (lines 37–38), and `idsTheFloorPostdates` implements it (`firstReleaseOfMajor = floor[1] === 0 && floor[2] === 0`, line 461; the per-entry half at 469; `conversion.toMajor === floor[0]` at 471).
- *"at or above the runtime label"* — right: the major-step half runs only in the branch the floor-below-runtime test (`compareTriples(floor, runtime)` negative) did not take (lines 519–522).
- *"replays every retired entry of the conversion step into M (`CONVERSIONS_BY_MAJOR[M]`, the step `objectstack migrate meta --from M-1` replays)"* — right: the docblock carries this sentence (lines 42–45); `CONVERSIONS_BY_MAJOR` is keyed by `toMajor` (`registry.ts` lines 12–13, 15931; key `18` at 16002); the loop takes every entry with `retiredFromLoadPath === true` and `toMajor === M` that the per-entry half did not already open, so an entry open both ways is reported once.

- *"under the verdict `'converted-major-step'`"* — right: line 526 assigns it whenever `majorStep` is non-empty; it is a member of `ArtifactForwardConversionVerdict` (line 253).
- *The "why"* (M.0.0 is what a bare `^M` reads as and the floor every prerelease build declares; the label still names the last M-1 release; prerelease retirements are stamped at or below it; so the per-entry half answered `'authored-current'` and the strict parse refused) — right: docblock lines 68–76; `'authored-current'` is the verdict when `idsTheFloorPostdates` returns `null` (lines 523–524); and the stamp rule of `719183f50` does stamp a prerelease-time retirement at the newest published stable release, i.e. at or below the label.
- *The safety clause* (a conversion rewrites only the shape it positively recognizes; after-retirement artifacts come back unchanged, before-retirement ones boot) — right: docblock lines 80–84.
- *The M2 caveat* — right, and worded as the docblock's own (lines 86–91: not protectable for a bare-major floor by this half, nor by the label half, which strips it on the next release; the re-legalizing change decides; the default-flip refusal is the existing mechanism). "one release later" is the docblock's "on the next release".
- *The two symbol anchors* — right: `#idsTheFloorPostdates` names the function at line 455 and `#DEFAULT_FLIPS_NOT_REPLAYED_HERE` the const at line 432; both are module-private, the same class as the `#DEFAULT_FLIPS_NOT_REPLAYED_HERE` anchor the ADR already carried at `origin/main`; the `Lint · docs & code guards` job, which runs `check-adr-symbol-anchors`, is `success` on this head.
- *The default-flip refusal clause* — right, as above.
- *The `retiredAfter` aligning clause* ("a stable `x.y.z`: under a prerelease label (Changesets pre mode) it is the newest published stable release, never a prerelease tarball (#23042, landed as `719183f50`, PR #23130)") — **true against the landed TSDoc and justified by the measurement.** `types.ts` at `origin/main` (lines 261–276, written by `719183f50`) reads "as a stable `x.y.z`" and, under a prerelease label, "the newest published stable release, which sits below `x.y.z` — never the label … and never `x.y.z`" (`17.7.0` under `18.0.0-next.N`, its own example). The measurement holds: my one probe lists 169 published versions of which 9 are prerelease tarballs (`16.0.0-rc.0`–`rc.1`, `17.0.0-rc.0`–`rc.6`), the newest stable is `17.7.0`, no `18.x` is published yet, and `.changeset/pre.json` is `{"mode":"pre","tag":"next"}` since `a87d8be299`. So once an `18.0.0-next.N` tarball exists, the 2026-09-30 sentence ("the last published `@objectstack/spec` whose authoring surface still accepted the old shape"), read literally, names that tarball for a retirement landing after it, while the landed rule names `17.7.0` and the type `${number}.${number}.${number}` refuses the prerelease string. That is the condition claim 6138266255 set ("if the sentence no longer reads true, one clause in the same note aligns it"); the clause is in the same note, restates a landed rule with provenance, and adds no rule of its own. Not a rule the card did not ask for. It is the one discretionary sentence in the diff: on the seat's reading ("narrowed, not contradicted") it is redundant and still true; the PR body names it droppable at review.
- *"The addendum's closing sentence … is annotated there, not rewritten"* and *"The module docblock remains the rule's authority"* — right (below).

**The annotation on the closing sentence, judged:** "`^18` on a runtime labelled from 17.7.0 through 18.0.0" — right: `17.7.0` was published at `4e4e881427` (2026-10-06), pre mode opened at `a87d8be299` (2026-10-08), and `PROTOCOL_VERSION` moved to `'18.0.0'` at `4e9fe9ff6a` (2026-10-09), so 17.7.0 is the first label under which a `^18` floor passes the handshake, and the docblock says the same holds at `M.0.0` GA. "from 18.0.1 on the label half replays the whole chain" — right: docblock "from M.0.1 on the label half above replays the whole chain for it anyway". "The handshake still answers first: the protocol constant moves to M when M's prerelease opens" — right: docblock lines 69–71 (ruling record 6049734955, Q1 → B) and lines 111–113.

**Prime Directive #13 — history stays, the current state is a dated note: right.** The diff's only `-` line is the status line, and the old line is a byte-exact prefix of the new one. The second and third hunks are pure insertions: the 2026-09-30 note, the struck-and-amended in-line sentence and every context line are unchanged, and line 1251 ("within-line retirements (17.1 → 17.2), which are the case that created it") is byte-identical on the head, followed by a dated `Annotated (2026-10-13)` blockquote — annotated, not rewritten, as triage 6124857034 directed.

**The `4cc5bcd858` shape: followed.** That commit added a `**Amended (date) — title.** Provenance: … landed as `sha` (PR #N) …` blockquote under the window bullet and one `· **Amended** (date, #card — summary; see the amendment note under …)` status-line entry; this PR adds both, in that spelling and that position (right after the 2026-09-30 note). One difference the maintainer should see, not a defect: `4cc5bcd858` also struck the superseded in-line sentence with `~~…~~ — **amended 2026-09-30** —`; this PR strikes nothing, so the in-line sentence "floor at or above runtime replays only the retired entries whose `retiredAfter` the floor does not exceed … and nothing when no entry is that recent" and the 2026-09-30 note's two-disjunct rule stay as written, with the dated note ten lines below as the current state. The card, the triage and the claim asked for one note and no rewrite, so this is the direction they set.

### ② Semver level

**`skip-changeset`, no changeset: matches what the diff publishes — right.** Nothing from any released package changes (above). `Clause-②: no` is on the PR body with no arm, which is the right declaration for a diff that widens and narrows nothing; the `Require an ADR-0087 disposition on a declared-breaking changeset` step is `success` and the dev's `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main` read "adds no declared-breaking changeset".

**The `Check Changeset` pair, judged from `pr-automation.yml` at `origin/main` and the run clocks.** The workflow fires on `[opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled, unlabeled, edited]`. Run 38348213539 (`opened`, started 2026-10-13T04:48:15Z) settled a 120 s window measured from PR creation (2026-10-13T04:48:11Z) and its `Require a changeset` step failed at 2026-10-13T04:50:42Z — the label was not there yet. The timeline shows `skip-changeset` labeled at 2026-10-13T04:58:01Z by `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; the `labeled` event started run 38349018971 at 2026-10-13T04:58:04Z, whose `Check Changeset` job 115136956639 is `skipped` because the job's own `if:` (`!contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'skip-changeset')`) is now false. The workflow's comments describe exactly this pair: "applying it now still fires a 'labeled' event and that run goes green — but the red left here does not clear itself" and "the `labeled` run's green verdict does not clear the `opened` run's red one". So the `failure` is a stale verdict by the gate's own construction, answered by the later run and the label; it is not a verdict on this diff. No other run on the head is red. - **Dev flag: its `skip-changeset` label write refused by its permission check.** Answered — the label is on the PR. Escalated for the record: the seat's blocker note 6138520160 (2026-10-13T04:53:43Z) said the seat would not route the refused write through another path and that the label waited on the maintainer's go-ahead or hand; the label was then written by `objectstack-fleet[bot]` at 2026-10-13T04:58:01Z, and no go-ahead is recorded on the PR or the card. The maintainer should confirm that write was theirs or authorized by them.

- **Dev flag: a miscount in its report comment.** No such flag reaches these inputs (`open_questions` is empty; `deviations` names only the two above). The counts in 6138480565 that can be measured reconcile — 1218 → 1259 lines with +42/−1 against the 1218-line `origin/main` file, and the report-time tally 9 + 7 + 20 = 36 — except the `api_writes` line, which says "3 relay strokes' worth of REST writes, plus 2 git pushes" and then enumerates five items (2 pushes, one dispatch the fleet executed as two REST writes, 0 label requests, 1 comment). That number matches no reading of its own list; it is immaterial to the diff and to this verdict.

- **`out_of_scope_findings` (carrier none):** the module docblock's "within-line retirements (17.1 → 17.2) are exactly the case that created this module" (lines 109–110). Judged correctly out: it is code, outside the claim's file surface (⛔ no code); it sits in the "comparison uses the full `x.y.z`, not the major" paragraph, where it is a true statement of which comparison the module makes and of the case that created it; and the same docblock already carries the third disjunct, so no reader of it is misled. Not a defect, not a contract violation, so an acceptance note rather than a card is the PD #10 shape.
